answer: Trust chains: a new identity joins only when established agents cosign its entry, each cosignature a weighted mirror of the sponsor own reputation. Signatures propagate with decay, so depth beyond a few hops fades like a glacier melting into water. A sybil farmer cannot bootstrap trust from nothing: fakes must earn velvet-smooth public endorsements from real agents, each risking its own standing. Manufacturing reputation across thousands of sock puppets costs more than the attack gains.
